title: Genesis Credit - Data residency & compliance discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency and compliance requirements for a conversational AI pilot. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of regulatory controls and logging restrictions; they asked detailed questions about region isolation, KMS integration, audit logs, and retention policies. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/HIPAA docs, schedule technical deep dive for SE to validate VPC networking and run a small benchmark, share pilot pricing options.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
next_steps: Sofia to share SOC2 and HIPAA whitepaper (by 2025-09-29)
Ethan to schedule technical deep dive with Priya & Tom (week of 2025-10-06)
Redwood to provide pilot pricing and dedicated capacity options (by 2025-10-01)
Customer to confirm success criteria and list of redacted PII examples (by 2025-09-30)
action_items: Owner: Sofia Patel | Item: Share SOC2 report + HIPAA attestation | Due: 2025-09-29
Owner: Ethan Kim | Item: Prepare VPC network diagram for Private deployment and example IAM policies | Due: 2025-10-03
Owner: Laura Martinez | Item: Send list of regulatory requirements and allowed log retention windows | Due: 2025-09-30
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-26 15:00 EDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Laura (Genesis Head of Data & AI), Tom (CISO), Priya (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm sofia from Redwood, i run the accounts for the finance vertical, um with me is ethan who's our solutions engineer. quick round robin?
[00:08] Laura: Hi, laura here. thanks, we are looking at adding a conversational layer to our customer support workflows, lots of regulatory constraints.
[00:13] Tom: Tom Reynolds, CISO. i'm mainly here for controls, logging, encryption, retention.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, platform engineer, i'll be owning the network and infra side.
[00:21] Ethan: Great, thanks. quick agenda: understand your residency/compliance constraints, map to deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), and identify next steps for a pilot.
[00:30] Laura: Sounds good. to start — high level — we are a US-headquartered credit union but have customers in EU and US, so GDPR matters. also we need to be HIPAA-aware for some co-borrower workflows, and of course a bunch of financial services controls — PCI-ish, audit trails, that kind of thing.
[00:47] Sofia: Understood. are you expecting to store any PHI or payment card numbers in the prompt layer, or will that be redacted upstream?
[00:55] Laura: Our plan is to redact most sensitive fields before hitting the model, but there will be PII and some account identifiers. we need guaranteed residency for EU customer records and strict logging retention policies.
[01:06] Tom: Right and from a security perspective we need: SOC 2 report, details on audit logs (what's captured, where it's stored, retention windows), KMS integration for keys, and the ability to run in a private VPC or on-prem if needed. also need to know about token-level exposure — are logs or raw requests stored in plaintext?
[01:28] Ethan: Good questions. short answers: for Redwood hosted we store minimal metadata by default and we have options for log redaction and short retention. for Dedicated you get isolated capacity and stricter controls; Private gives you customer-managed networking and full control over storage. regarding keys, we support KMS/HSM integrations and bring-your-own-keys for both Dedicated and Private.
[01:47] Laura: Can you clarify region isolation for hosted? can we guarantee EU data stays in EU for processing and logs?
[01:54] Sofia: For our hosted product we have regional endpoints — you can pin requests to eu-west, us-east, etc., and we can restrict storage to those regions. however, the default hosted offering does aggregate some telemetry for product improvements unless you opt out — that's usually not acceptable for strict residency cases.
[02:13] Priya: So if we need enforced residency and strict logging controls, hosted may be tricky. Dedicated — is that multi-tenant or is it fully isolated?
[02:22] Ethan: Dedicated is single-customer capacity, logically isolated GPU pools, and you get separate storage buckets. It's still managed by Redwood but with contractual guarantees around location and retention. Private is the full separation option — control plane can be private and the inference plane can be deployed inside your VPC or on-prem.
[02:40] Tom: About logging: we need to capture request id, requester, timestamps, but we cannot capture full prompt text for longer than X days. what retention windows do you support?
[02:49] Ethan: We can configure retention policies down to 0 days for raw transcripts — basically configure immediate redaction of prompt text and retain only metadata for up to 90 days or longer depending on contract. for Dedicated/Private, retention windows are contract-configurable.
[03:06] Laura: What about audit trails for regulators? we need signed, immutable logs and exportable for audits — S3 or syslog integration would be ideal.
[03:15] Ethan: We offer export hooks to customer-managed S3 buckets, and we can stream audit logs to syslog or SIEMs. we also support append-only object stores and can integrate with your logging pipeline.
[03:28] Priya: Network bits: if we do Private in our AWS account, how do you handle egress/back-and-forth? do we need peering or is there a connector?
[03:36] Ethan: For Private we support VPC peering and VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) — traffic stays within the region. we'll provide a tech diagram for the setup. for on-prem, we have a package but it requires some ops collaboration.
[03:49] Tom: Encryption — at-rest and in-transit, but specifically KMS — can we use our existing KMS keys?
[03:55] Sofia: Yes, bring-your-own-key is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys by default but we have a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise tiers.
[04:06] Laura: Any third-party logging or telemetry going to Redwood R&D? like for model improvement?
[04:12] Ethan: By default we may collect telemetry, but for enterprise customers we can disable telemetry collection and opt out of model improvement data. we can also provide an agreement clause.
[04:22] Laura: Good. On compliance: do you have HIPAA attestation and can you sign BAAs?
[04:27] Sofia: We have HIPAA-supporting controls and can sign a BAA for Dedicated/Private deployments. we'll share the HIPAA whitepaper.
[04:33] Tom: SOC 2 type II?
[04:35] Sofia: yes, SOC 2 type II. i'll share the report.
[04:37] Priya: So from a timeline perspective — the business wants to run a pilot in Q4. minimal viable is a hosted pilot but we need assurances for EU residency and log redaction. is that feasible?
[04:48] Ethan: Hosted could work if you opt out of telemetry and pin region endpoints, but if you require guaranteed auditors' access to immutable logs and BYOK, i'd recommend Dedicated — it's our most common for financial pilots.
[05:00] Laura: Cost/latency tradeoff — we care about latency for chat in the app. Dedicated would be better for predictable latency but is more expensive. any recommendations?
[05:09] Ethan: If you have 50–100 QPS at peak, Dedicated gives you predictable tail latency and better throughput. hosted is cheaper but variable. for pilot scale, Dedicated light (small reserved pool) usually works — we can size it for expected load.
[05:23] Tom: Are there controls to scrub PII before logs are persisted? we want deterministic redaction.
[05:29] Ethan: Yes, we have pre-send hooks for redaction and token filters. you can run redaction at the customer gateway or within the inference path and then configure log retention to not store raw prompts.
[05:40] Laura: Can we do a canary where a percentage of traffic goes to hosted and the rest to Dedicated?
[05:45] Sofia: Absolutely — we support routing policies and traffic splits by route so you can do canary and gradual rollouts.
[05:51] Priya: For benchmarks — we'd want a small set of synthetic and real-ish prompts to test latency and cost. can Redwood run that in our region?
[05:59] Ethan: Yes, we can run benchmarks in-region. for Dedicated/Private we can run on the actual capacity. for hosted we can provide regionally pinned endpoints and run test harnesses. we'll need a sample prompt set and expected SLAs.
[06:10] Tom: Any regulatory blockers with EU citizens' data being processed in the US?
[06:15] Sofia: For GDPR you either keep EU personal data within EU region endpoints or establish appropriate safeguards (SCCs if processing outside). Dedicated and Private are the simplest for residency. we can include SCC language in contracts.
[06:28] Laura: Ok. On the security questionnaire — we have a long vendor risk assessment. can you provide standard attachments (SOC2, penetration test summary, architecture diagram)?
[06:37] Sofia: Yes, we'll send SOC2 report, summary of pen test, network diagram, and our data processing addendum.
[06:43] Priya: We also have restrictions on logs — max 30 days for raw prompts, meta-data retained up to 365 days. is that configurable?
[06:50] Ethan: Yes, retention windows are configurable in Dedicated/Private via policy; hosted has some limits but enterprise tiers can customize. we'll capture your retention spec in the next steps.
[07:00] Laura: A couple of nitty-gritty things: do you store KV cache or prompt caches outside the region? and what about model snapshots for debugging — are those retained?
[07:12] Ethan: KV caches can be configured to live in-region; default behavior keeps them ephemeral and not stored long-term. model snapshots used for debugging are only stored if you opt-in; otherwise we store metrics and traces not raw inputs.
[07:25] Tom: One more compliance ask — ability to disable 3rd-party analytics and prevent any PII going to external vendors.
[07:31] Sofia: We can disable external analytics for enterprise. we'll include contractual guarantees.
[07:34] Laura: Great. Let's talk about pilot success criteria: accuracy on redacted prompts, latency under 350ms p50, no raw prompt retention, region isolation for EU, and audit export available.
[07:46] Sofia: That sounds good. Ethan, can you propose an architecture for Dedicated pilot and list the infra needs?
[07:52] Ethan: Yes — propose small dedicated GPU pool in us-east and eu-west, VPC peering for private connect, KMS integration, S3 log bucket in customer account, and audit exports. i'll draft the diagram.
[08:04] Priya: For the Private option if we host in our VPC, what's required from our side?
[08:09] Ethan: We'll need an account role for deployment, network peering, and some outbound access for control plane if you choose managed control plane. for fully air-gapped on-prem we have a separate package and it's heavier.
[08:21] Laura: Timeline check — if we sign pilot next week, can we be live in 3–4 weeks?
[08:26] Sofia: For Dedicated pilot yes, typically 3–6 weeks depending on procurement. Private can take longer (4–8 weeks) because of networking.
[08:35] Tom: Procurement — we'll need an MSA and DPA and BAA options. can you send template agreements?
[08:41] Sofia: Yes. we'll share MSA, DPA, BAA and SCC templates.
[08:45] Laura: Anything surprising about retention or backups we should be aware of?
[08:49] Ethan: Not beyond what we've discussed. backups for Dedicated can be disabled or kept within customer-only buckets.
[08:56] Priya: Operationally, who do we contact during onboarding for infra support?
[08:59] Sofia: Your AE is the primary contact — Ethan will be the SE. during onboarding you'll get a named onboarding engineer and an escalation path.
[09:07] Laura: ok great. before we wrap any open questions?
[09:11] Tom: One: do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for the console and API access?
[09:15] Sofia: Yes SSO, SAML, and fine grained RBAC — supported for enterprise.
[09:19] Priya: Do you provide per-route cost breakdowns for token usage?
[09:23] Ethan: Yes, we have per-route/model dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[09:27] Laura: ok good. quick recap: send docs (SOC2, HIPAA, MSA/DPA/BAA), draft pilot architecture and pricing, schedule technical deep dive.
[09:36] Sofia: perfect. we'll send the package and calendar invite for the SE deep dive.
[09:40] Tom: thanks everyone.
[09:42] End of transcript (note: transcription contains occasional mishears; confirm critical legal language from attachments).
